name: Medieval Kingdom painted isometric
summary: Pre-rendered 3D forms shown in the game's 2:1 isometric projection. Weathered stone, warm timber and muted earth, lit by one late-morning sun from the front left. Readable silhouettes first, texture second.

projection.screenAxes: grid x runs right-down, grid y runs left-down, height runs up

stone.description: Coursed field stone with dark mortar lines. Main walls of towers, keeps and walls.

stone_light.description: Dressed limestone for important buildings and trims.

stone_dark.description: Foundations, plinths and wet lower courses.

wood.description: Sawn timber: galleries, hoardings, walls of huts.

roof_tile.description: Fired clay roofs for wealthy buildings.

thatch.description: Straw roofs of farms and peasant houses.

opening.description: Arrow slits and dark window openings.

banner.description: Cloth banners in the kingdom colour.

rock.description: Natural rock outcrops and quarry faces.

light.rule: One sun for every asset, from the front left. The left-front face is brightest, the right-front face is mid-tone, roofs catch the most light. Shadows fall back-right and are baked into the sprite at 32 % opacity.

detail.silhouette: Readable at 1x game zoom. Prefer two or three strong masses over many small parts.
detail.outline: No drawn outlines. Separation comes from the light contrast between faces.
detail.textureScale: One texture tile covers the material's repeat in world units: bricks about 0.3 × 0.15 units (13 × 6 px at 1×), boards about 0.17 units wide, shingle rows about 0.12 units. Detail therefore matches across assets.
detail.colour: Use palette materials only. New colours need a palette entry first.

day.label: Day
day.description: Neutral. Sprites are authored for this state.

dusk.label: Dusk
dusk.description: Warm, slightly darker; torches start to read.

night.label: Night
night.description: Cool blue darkness; torches and fires carry the scene.

lightingModel: Sprites carry daylight only. Time of day is applied at runtime by multiplying the scene with a light map: the light map is filled with the ambient colour and each light source is added as a coloured radial gradient. Flames are drawn after the multiply so they stay bright. No per-time-of-day sprites.

rules: Animated parts are separate layers or frames anchored to the same sprite anchor.
Flames, smoke and banners animate; buildings stay static.
Units use eight directions with the same projection and light as buildings.
Loops must be seamless and last 4 to 12 frames.

terrain.rule: Ground is a flat 64 × 32 tile texture. Tiles of one set share a periodic colour field, so any two of them join without a seam.
terrain.grass: Lively mid-greens with darker patches; blades 2–9 px at 1×, drawn as small tufts; flowers sparse and pale. Avoid yellow-brown dry grass as the default.
terrain.paths: Wear goes from green through flattened dark green and olive to muted dark brown soil. Each stage is darker than the one before; no orange, red or bright tan (chroma at most 0.24).
terrain.overgrowth: An unused path recovers stage by stage back to grass (src/data/pathWear.js: recovery after 3 days, 5 points a day), so every stage must also read as a path growing over.
